OTTAVA names Memorial Hermann as its first commercial customer

Johnson & Johnson selects a former clinical trial site for the start of its early-access commercial program.

RobotsBeat ↗21 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

The new development

Johnson & Johnson announced on November 19 that Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center in Houston will be the first hospital to install OTTAVA under its early-access commercial program. The hospital previously evaluated the platform in clinical trials, marking a transition from research collaboration to a commercial customer relationship.

Technology and applications

OTTAVA integrates four robotic arms into a standard-sized surgical table, an architecture intended to address operating-room space and workflow constraints. It received US FDA authorization in July 2026 for multiple general-surgery procedures in the upper abdomen. The announcement does not describe a robot operating independently of surgeons.

Scope and next steps

The company plans a selective US rollout while gathering real-world evidence. Pricing and a detailed installation schedule were not disclosed. A first customer is a commercial milestone, while effects on operating-room time, costs and patient outcomes still require assessment using additional clinical and operational data.
